the rapporteur. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, in the last year the number of refugees in the world has increased and we are already at about 12 million. if we add up the internally displaced, we have more than 26 million people in need of protection worldwide. the reason for this situation is that there are still wars on the planet. there are now four million refugees and displaced persons from iraq, and it is clear that these refugees are the result of wars that our countries have also wanted. the creation of a common european asylum system is necessary because it is an obligation for our rule of law to ensure homogeneity in the reception of the european union, all the more so if we consider that there are member states which do not yet have an organic asylum law. i regret that the harmonization of asylum procedures has been delayed by two years, so that we will have harmonization in 2012. the harmful disparity between countries, between asylum systems, must be ended. it is paradoxical that at the moment there are some third country nationals whose refugee status is granted at rates ranging from 0% to 90%, depending on the member state receiving the application. the harmonization of standards must result in a high level of protection throughout the european union and not in a leveling down. the institution of asylum is an essential aspect of our democracy and the protection of human rights, and it is unacceptable that it has been seriously undermined in recent years, because the needs of asylum seekers and the principle of non-refoulement guaranteed by international conventions have not always been guaranteed. the european union should provide for mechanisms at the external borders to identify asylum seekers and to ensure access to its territory for persons eligible for international protection, including in the context of border control operations. that is why we think it is appropriate to review the role of frontex, which often treats asylum seekers as irregular migrants. the european parliament, in this report, asks that frontex provide precise data on the number of asylum seekers detected during the operations carried out and also on the fate of persons intercepted and returned to countries of transit or countries of origin. the correct application of international conventions must be ensured, including cooperation agreements with third countries. we cannot make agreements with countries that have not signed the geneva convention, and many member countries do: i am thinking of italy, which has signed an agreement with libya on the management of migration flows, and which does not intend to sign the geneva convention on refugees. we are very pleased - and we have stressed this and we want to stress this in this report - that the court of justice has annulled the article of the 'procedure directive' which concerned the establishment of the concept of 'safe third countries' and the common list of safe third countries. we believe that there can be no such thing as a 'safe third country', that the concept is inappropriate, because all citizens can be persecuted even in countries with high standards of democracy. asylum seekers are vulnerable people who must be provided with appropriate reception conditions. member states may not detain a person solely on the ground that he or she is an applicant for international protection. i therefore believe that asylum seekers should not in principle be detained, and unfortunately in many member states detention of asylum seekers is still a reality, because of their illegal entry into the territory. unfortunately, and i conclude, there is no other way to enter the european union. and this is the paradox: i would like to ask the commissioner whether he is aware that the commission has not yet taken a decision on the matter. childcare is not a concession. asylum is a duty of countries and a right of people fleeing war.
vice-president of the commission. - madam president, i will be brief, but i listened carefully to all the speeches and i am very grateful to the european parliament for its support for this effort to give asylum policy the full scope it should have for all the people who are persecuted in the world. we have a duty, a moral imperative, as martine roure used to say. i would like to make a few points. first of all, some of you have mentioned frontex, mr catania in particular. i should like to point out that frontex now has a liaison officer with the united nations high commissioner for refugees. this is really an effort by frontex to get a good grasp of the problems affecting asylum seekers, and the commission has proposed rules to better define frontex's responsibilities in maritime actions. we are currently discussing this with the member states. that is an important element, indeed. i would like to return to the request for solidarity that has been expressed by many of you, and i am thinking in particular of mr busuttil, who has mentioned the difficult situation in malta in this respect. it is true that in the action plan on asylum the commission proposed to study the possibilities of distributing these asylum seekers among the member states on a voluntary basis. the discussion with the member states was launched in the autumn with an informal document proposing several alternatives for implementing the principle of solidarity in the field of asylum. i must say that it is not easy to get the majority of member states to agree on a mechanism for allocating refugees among them. we will nevertheless launch a study on the impact and possibilities of this type of distribution at union level. i would also like to say that we are ready to finance projects relating to this distribution, to this resettlement, under the european refugee fund. i shall have the opportunity to repeat this in the member states i shall visit, which are often very popular with asylum seekers. in short, i believe that we are at the beginning of a long process, but one which is essential if we really want this europe to retain in its values a strong identity, an identity as a region of welcome for all those who, in the world, are suffering and are waiting for our help. i would like to thank the european parliament, madam president, ladies and gentlemen, for all your speeches, which are particularly valuable to your commissioner.
the rapporteur. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to thank the members who have spoken for their support for this report, commissioner barrot for his support and also for the work that the commission is doing in view of the amendments to certain directives, and in particular the procedure and reception directive, which demonstrate the commission's willingness to improve the common asylum system. parliament is a co-legislator in this area and i believe that we must play our part in harmonizing asylum procedures upwards, towards a system of harmonization which has wide margins of reception, improves the standards of reception in the member states, making it ever more supportive. i believe that this parliament has played an important role in visiting the administrative detention centres in europe. we visited many of them - mrs roure was rapporteur for the final report - and we were able to see how often the right to asylum was violated in the member states, how often the normal reception conditions, the right to health, to legal assistance, and even to information on potential asylum seekers were not guaranteed. this is because mixed flows have been managed by putting the fight against irregular immigration and the protection of the external borders ahead of the need to welcome and in particular to receive asylum seekers. i agree with what some of my colleagues have said, particularly on the need to review the dublin regulation, particularly on the need to ensure a solidarity mechanism between countries for burden sharing, but also a solidarity mechanism towards asylum seekers, so that they are also given the right to be transferred to another place so that their application can be accepted. finally, i would like to conclude by saying that some of my colleagues have raised the issue of border control. i think that's a fundamental flaw in the reasoning. the issue of border protection and the right of asylum are two issues that are not compatible with each other. we must guarantee the right to asylum, as it is a fundamental right which must be guaranteed by the european union.
in writing. while in italy the government has had a non-linear approach to the roma issue, and at times very questionable in terms of humanitarian principles, in europe it has always worked to maintain the difficult balance between integration and security. the european parliament's resolution on the social situation of the roma and their access to the european labour market goes in this direction. it is clear that the repeated use of emergency legislative measures to address roma-related problems indicates an inability to address a not new phenomenon. instead, organic approaches and long-term coordinated solutions are needed in education, health care and especially labour market policies because employment and education in turn promote social acceptance and integration. europe calls for an end to the discriminatory practice of evicting roma from camps by developing concrete social housing projects that can address the housing problem of this community. in short, we need coherent policy choices which, combining solidarity and responsibility, allow us to deal with an emergency that otherwise risks getting out of hand. there is a proper awareness that this is a difficult road to travel, but there are no alternatives to these routes.
member of the commission. - the madam president, i am pleased that we are discussing today the proposal for a recast of the directive on industrial emissions and i would like to thank in particular the rapporteur, mr krahmer, and the committee on the environment, public health and food safety for their excellent work on this dossier. i would also like to thank the committee on legal affairs and citizens' rights for its positive contribution. in recent weeks the commission has gathered reliable evidence that the current directive on integrated pollution prevention and control is not being sufficiently implemented and that industrial emissions remain at excessively high levels. this situation has caused serious negative effects on the environment and the health of european citizens. it also distorts competition between european industries. this unacceptable situation must be brought to an end. the best available techniques are a key component of the integrated approach on which the directive is based. these techniques have significant environmental and economic benefits. in principle, they reduce emissions and limit the use of resources, thus contributing to the long-term improvement of the security of energy supply of the european union. they also provide incentives for eco-innovation, which is essential for european industry to be able to meet future global demand for environmental technologies. to take full advantage of the advantages of best available techniques, their application framework needs to be strengthened and improved. the commission proposal is aimed at this. it clarifies and upgrades the role of best available techniques reference documents, so-called brefs, in the implementation of legislation. this will bring the conditions for licensing businesses across the european union closer together and, by extension, bring competition conditions closer together. brefs shall be drawn up through a transparent process with the broad involvement of member states, industry and other relevant actors. the efforts required for their preparation and approval are considerable. we must support the process of adopting them and the institution of brefs in general. brefs will thus be able to play a greater role in setting the conditions for the granting of licences to industrial enterprises, which will result in our industrial plants meeting the highest possible environmental requirements set by european union legislation. the commission proposal provides the necessary flexibility for deviations from the brefs, provided of course that this is justified by local circumstances. however, detailed justification and documentation of any deviation is necessary to avoid any abuse. at the same time, minimum mandatory requirements should be laid down at european union level for certain industrial sectors with particularly serious environmental impacts. in addition, few minimum standards have already been established for sectors such as large combustion plants or waste incinerators. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. although mandatory minimum requirements may be considered useful for certain industrial sectors, it is not certain that the setting of minimum standards is necessary or appropriate for all sectors. minimum standards should be established only if and when they are necessary and justified from an environmental point of view. a typical example is the large combustion plant sector, which is responsible for a significant share of air pollution. the best available techniques are far from being properly applied in this particular sector. for this reason, the commission has proposed new minimum requirements for large combustion plants based on the conclusions of the relevant bref. they are expected to be implemented in 2016. these measures will make a significant contribution to achieving the relevant objectives of the thematic strategy on air pollution in an economically viable manner. moreover, the net benefit of these requirements at both european union and national level outweighs the related costs. finally, in addition to improving the implementation of the directive, the main objective of its recast is to simplify legislation and reduce administrative costs for both industry and the competent authorities, always in line with the principles of the european union's programme to improve legislation. the proposal therefore merges seven existing legislative acts into a single directive. this will also improve the clarity and consistency of the legislation for both member states and businesses. the benefits of this simplification are manifold. reducing pollution from industrial installations is a key priority for both environmental and economic reasons. the proposal submitted will simplify the existing legislation and at the same time strengthen the framework for the application of best available techniques. this will further contribute to improving environmental protection and the sustainability of european industry. i therefore look forward to hearing your views on this important proposal and the constructive dialogue that will follow.
i believe that this directive is, as has been said, the most important instrument for controlling industrial pollution that this parliament has discussed since the climate and energy package. the time is probably not the most fortunate, because of the financial crisis, which is putting pressure on the industrial system and which has therefore led to excessive lobbying by companies towards parliamentary groups, worried about the financial implications of this directive, as of the previous climate-energy package. we are comforted by the fact that we are still at first reading and that therefore perhaps some corrections and improvements will still be possible to recover at second reading. i have to say to mr krahmer: it wasn't an easy process. the rapporteur, mr krahmer, criticised the position of the epp, which called into question some of the compromises. but i would like to point out that 60 amendments have been tabled, of which less than a third were tabled by members of the european people's party. so there is a widespread desire in the european parliament to discuss some of the relevant points of this directive and unfortunately there has been no meeting between the rapporteur and the shadow rapporteur in the last few days to discuss the 60 amendments. we must not forget that the directive arises from the fact that the previous directive has not been easy to implement in the member states until now. we have seen an excessive diversification in the control and analysis regime which, as mr krahmer said, needs to be corrected. but the european commission also needs to make a greater effort. brefs have too long processing times and therefore do not ensure transparency in the application of the directive. it is true that there is a very strong process of collaboration and involvement of industry, but a more rapid periodic approval of brefs also ensures greater protection of the health of citizens. i would also add that there has certainly been little investment by industrialists in the past: i believe that, since too many people in europe are getting sick and dying from air pollution caused by industrial emissions, we must take action with appropriate clean-up measures and a strong control and analysis system.

member of the commission. − mr president, i would like to thank all the members who have participated in today’s debate. they have made a constructive contribution to it. i would especially like to thank the rapporteur, mr krahmer, for his excellent hard work. before i close, i would like to say a few words on some of the key amendments that have been discussed today. firstly, i welcome your broad support for the thrust of the commission’s proposal and, in particular, for the strengthening of the application of best available techniques (bat) and the status of the bref documents. this is the cornerstone of the commission’s proposal. there are many amendments that are acceptable to the commission, at least in part or in principle. in particular, many of the amendments help to clarify the text of the commission’s proposal or to improve transparency in the development of the brefs and in the permitting and enforcement practices of member states. better information and participation of the public in these decisions is very welcome. i also share the concerns expressed on the need to avoid the misuse of flexibility in setting permit conditions. as i mentioned earlier, minimum requirements can be very useful and necessary tools to tackle specific problems where certain sectors have not taken the necessary steps to implement bat. however, the systematic setting of minimum requirements is not necessary and risks creating an additional administrative burden for little environmental gain. therefore, i consider that minimum standards should only be set where needed to achieve a better implementation of bat. in considering minimum requirements on large combustion plants, it is important to keep in mind the significant impacts that such operations have on the environment and on the health of european union citizens. bat for large combustion plants was agreed in 2006 and it is the commission’s view that the minimum criteria should be applied from 2016. we need to ensure that the measures put in place for the sector bring it into line with bat at the earliest opportunity and facilitate the achievement of the objectives set out in the thematic strategy on air pollution. another key element to ensure that the legislation is effective in its objectives is that of the provisions for compliance and enforcement measures. in the past we have identified some shortcomings in this regard and it is, therefore, of paramount importance that the new legislation sets clear provisions to ensure the law is properly implemented. for this reason, the commission’s proposal introduces minimum provisions for inspection, review of permit conditions and reporting of compliance. these changes will ensure the proper implementation of bat and reduce distortions in competition. the commission will be extremely vigilant on this issue. i would like to say a few words about the thresholds for intensive agricultural farms, mainly poultry. the same threshold is currently applied for all poultry, without taking into account the different types of species. the rearing of different species leads to different environmental impacts, in particular due to the different weight of the animals. the proposed new thresholds have been set on the basis of the environmental impact of the species concerned. the new thresholds would include a limited number of additional farms compared to the current scope, and would reduce ammonia emissions in a cost efficient manner to meet the objectives of the thematic strategy on air pollution, in some areas. i will provide parliament’s secretariat with a list detailing the commission’s position on the amendments. commission’s position on amendments by parliament krahmer report (a6-0046/2009) the commission can support fully, in part, or in principle amendments 1, 5-8, 12-14, 16, 18-21, 27, 34-37, 40, 42-44, 46, 48-56, 58-62, 64-66, 68, 69, 71-73, 75 and 79. the amendments which the commission cannot support are amendments 2-4, 9-11, 15, 17, 22-26, 28-33, 38, 39, 41, 45, 47, 57, 63, 67, 70, 76-78, 80, 93, 97, 114, 115, 117, 129 and 133.

vice-president of the commission. − mr president, i should like to thank the members for an interesting debate and for their many valuable comments. regulation (ec) no 1049/2001 will now be updated to ‘version two’, one might say. it is important to point out again that we are not starting from scratch: we already have a good basis, and it is just a matter of improving on that. this will also be a version for the age of the internet, as was mentioned in the debate. electronic registers will now be included, and add to that active dissemination, as examples of these improvements. the ideal situation would, of course, be for us to disseminate information so actively that no requests for access have to be made since everything is already out there – with some exceptions, of course. i can give you one example of what can be done, which is that i have already made my own correspondence register available on the internet, so you can see my correspondence and documents. it is not possible for me to go through all the comments that were made during the debate, but i want to comment briefly on a few crucial points, one of which concerns the definition of documents under article 3. this is one of the articles of the commission’s proposal that have been most discussed and, i admit, most criticised. we maintain that the current definition leads to ambiguity and a risk of unpredictability and bad practice. is this post-it note a document, for example? mr cashman is saying it is, and according to the wide definition in the regulation, it could very well be so – as could the other scribbles i have here. sometimes it is not helpful to make a definition too broad. we still maintain a wide definition, but we will reduce the discretionary non-disclosure of documents. the definition that we propose is much wider than the notion of official documents often used in national legislation. it comes very close to the concept of information in the uk freedom of information act and in the dutch law on transparency, for example. the registration of documents is an obligation under internal commission rules, but these do not determine whether a document falls within the scope of the regulation. so we clarified and helped with the definition of documents. this will also help citizens to know what is it you can and should ask for in order to get full information. a more precise definition of documents means safer administration and more clarity for citizens. the court has ruled that documents relating to an ongoing investigation are manifestly covered by an exception to the right of access and, therefore, that those files are currently not acceptable and this does not constitute additional restriction of the right of access. in no member state do citizens have access to the files of the competition authorities – i just wanted to make that point. i also acknowledge that we could have explained and phrased things better in article 3. i believe we share the same goal, and thus it should also be possible to find a clear and unambiguous wording. this is an example of an area where we should be able to achieve a good compromise text. another fiercely discussed point is article 5(2) concerning access to member states’ documents. let me be clear that the commission’s intention has been to implement what the european court of justice has ruled, and member states must effectively justify why they refuse access to one of their documents, just as the institutions do regarding all other documents. the bottom line will always be the rules in regulation (ec) no 1049/2001. however, it is equally important that the commission can have correspondence with member states, for example in the field of infringements of eu law. we need to have the possibility to quickly find satisfactory solutions from the perspective of both the commission and eu citizens, as codified by eu law. those kinds of contacts need to remain confidential, and that is also what the court has said. finally, i shall just comment on the ‘space to think’ under article 4(3). if we think carefully, i guess most people would agree that parliament, as well as the commission and the council, needs a certain space to think. documents related to decisions that have not yet been taken, or reflecting internal discussions, are not the same as other documents. what about the records of political group meetings or preparations? you have yourselves identified a number of problems and limitations arising from refusing a space to think, considering, again, what would benefit citizens most and what would be most helpful. i must say that i would have preferred the council to be here – as many of you have said – just as i would have preferred a fuller house, because these are absolutely crucial issues for all of us. the big task for us all in the next few weeks or months is to find common ground. that is also true within this house, and today’s debate has shown that it is not always that easy. the more divisions there are, the more difficult it will be when the three institutions hold discussions. parliament, the council and the commission each have their role, which should be respected, and i hope parliament will speak with one strong voice, because that will benefit us all and benefit the end result, which i hope will be a balanced and workable compromise text.

in writing. - thank you, mr president. since the schengen treaty came into force, much progress has been made. the treaty has radically changed the lives of many europeans by bringing a new idea of border management to the fore. in 2002, the new phase of integrated border management was launched, leading to the establishment of a common body of legislation, a common system of consultation, operational cooperation, a common integrated risk assessment, trained staff and burden-sharing between member states with a view to a european border guard corps. now that this phase is over, it is time to look ahead to achieving truly integrated border management, to achieve the dual objective of improving security and facilitating travel procedures for third country nationals. i therefore welcome the proposals which the commission has put before parliament, many of which have already been dealt with in my report on the community code on the rules governing the crossing of frontiers. at this point it seems inevitable to continue along this path, giving our favourable opinion to the creation of a system of entry/exit registration, facilitating the crossing of borders for travellers and the introduction of an electronic travel authorization system.

the rapporteur. mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, tonight, this evening, we are concluding a long session of work and i think that each of us should be satisfied with the results achieved. for various reasons, which are those which concern the union as a whole, because it is clear that allowing the european union to create regional regulatory spaces where there are international rules governing them, to interfere between the member states and international organizations in defining rules, is an activity that should be done only when this is necessary. and it was obviously necessary: the incidents that set the process in motion have made this unfortunately clear. the result achieved is one which, i believe, cannot fail to satisfy everyone, in the sense that it is an honourable compromise of a long process, in which all the institutions involved - the commission, parliament, the council - have played their part, each, so to speak, representing the interests which they are called upon to represent. this is why the whole sector, the whole framework of maritime safety has today taken a step forward. in short, my colleagues and i have had the honour and opportunity to deal with more specific problems: i have had the responsibility and the pleasure of dealing with the liability of the carriers, the carriers, in the event of accidents to the people carried on board. i must of course admit that, as always, the result is a halfway house between the ambitions we have expressed, ambitions which at one time even seemed capable of being achieved: the ambition was to immediately extend cover, protection to all those who board a ship, whether it is on international seas, on national seas or along rivers. then, as it were, the reality of things meant that the scope was partly reduced. i acknowledge, let us say, but i cannot help but point out that something is missing from this set of rules, because many of the ships that pass indifferently from inside a river to the sea are not covered in this way and surely this is a point that will have to be covered in some way; i am sure that the commission will take action in this direction as soon as possible. we have also set a long enough period for domestic sea travel to be covered. this problem of length is a problem of transition periods, perhaps it is a theme that we have underestimated. i am afraid that the risk we have is that they are too long and that we will therefore have to wait too long for this. but it's better to have them than to have nothing different. the other big point under discussion - and yet the point reached - is that this protection starts from a safe moment. of course, we can now tell our citizens that when they board a ship they are covered, in essence, from the end of 2012, however they move. in short, we have also made all citizens feel a little more european in this respect, because the same coverage will be available on every sea, in every place, for every ship.
mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, parliament and the committee on transport could not and cannot fail to deal with the matter of improving the safety of ships and also to specify the measures to be taken in the event of an accident. the third maritime package also effectively addresses the issues of the responsibilities of carriers towards passengers and the goods they carry. it was now, always hoping that the matter would not end up being ignored, as i have the impression that it is in the case of airline passenger rights. i believe that the targets for compliance by 2016 for category a vessels and the subsequent initiative for category b, c and d vessels are far too tolerant and too favourable to carriers. i hope that the union's generosity will be reflected in the timely adaptation of carriers to the new rules. common standards were and are also needed for classification societies responsible for the inspection of ships and the granting of navigation authorizations, as well as very clear rules for regulating inspections and blacklisting ships. i therefore welcome the proposals and the measures on the management of accidents and the risks of marine and environmental disasters and the expertise in this area, and i would perhaps ask the commission to do more. the package also includes measures relating to investigations, jurisdiction and due process in the event of a maritime incident, a compendium which we hope will help to clarify liability and compensation. i therefore vote in favour of the report as a whole.

the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of the environment is a very important one, and i would like to thank the rapporteur for the work he has done. we wrote then that water must be a human right and that active policies must be developed to realize this right through forms of public-public cooperation, which look in particular at local communities. unfortunately, that resolution was not supported by the european commission in mexico city - i remind the commissioner of that now - although it was very much appreciated by many countries, particularly in latin america. it is a matter of the very nature of this type of forum, which is a private structure. we will now have the opportunity to be present in istanbul as a parliamentary delegation and it would be good if our presence was supported by a resolution as appropriate as the one in 2006: we are not there yet, and i am therefore going to table amendments on that. we need a decisive change in the water problem. the figures for water suffering are well known and dramatic, and are set to worsen as a result of climate change. it is precisely in connection with climate change that the new field of action must be opened up. climate change is making access to water worse, and poor access to water is making climate change worse. so, to the issue of law, to the issue of public-public cooperation, we add the issue of a strong relationship to be established with the kyoto protocol. the un must be involved in the water issue. it is to a special un structure that the world water governance can be entrusted, removing it from the privateist logic that is still present in the current forum. and it would also help to connect with the big conventions, the climate convention and the desertification convention, which are living right in the un. of course, we also need adequate funding, which can come from general taxation and levies, for example, on mineral waters, which - i would like to say to my colleagues - we are also abusing in this parliament. the privatization of water must be opposed: it would make access to a vital good no longer a right but a market. and i think that our whole european history teaches us that it is the public that has guaranteed the right to water in our homes, which is not the case in other continents that are increasingly reliant on private penetration. these are practical issues, but they are also of great moral value. it is no coincidence that the right to water is being fought for by large movements, by large personalities, both secular and religious. the european parliament's chamber has recently been made available - we now have a short presentation of a series of reports on the agenda, eight in all, so i would ask all members to observe the time limits for this particular procedure scrupulously and i would also ask the commission to keep to the essentiality of the replies, otherwise we would have problems in respecting the agenda even for the assistance of interpreters. the agenda includes the report by alain hutchinson, on behalf of the committee on development, on contracts relating to the millennium development goals (mdgs) [2008/2128 ((ini)) ] (a6-0085/2009).
member of the commission. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i should like to begin by thanking the committee on development and its rapporteur, mr hutchinson, for this report, which contains a number of considerations and concerns which we fully share. more aid and better development aid are needed if we are to achieve the millennium development goals by 2015, but also much more predictable and less volatile aid, as your report very rightly points out. these efforts will obviously be made through a combination of multiple instruments, but in countries where this is possible, budgetary support, general or sectoral, remains in my view the most appropriate and appropriate instrument. budget support is best placed to strengthen national processes and systems, improve country ownership, facilitate harmonisation, reduce transaction costs and thus improve public expenditure management and accelerate the achievement of the development goals. the commission has already greatly increased the use of budgetary support and will do so even more over the next six years, under the 10th european development fund. it is to make this instrument more effective and predictable that the commission has, in consultation with the member states and other stakeholders, devised a longer-term form of budget support which we have called the mdg contract for countries which meet certain criteria: good past performance, sound management of public finances, appropriate sectoral policy, etc. the mdg contract is the natural evolution of general budget support, not only because of its greater predictability but above all because of its focus on results and its ability to have a graduated response based on performance. these are partner countries which have committed themselves to focusing their policies and thus their expenditure on the millennium development goals. the mdg contract offers the following key elements: a six-year commitment, i.e. all six years against a previously customary three-year duration of general budget support; a fixed guaranteed payment of at least 70% of total commitments provided that there is no break in the eligibility conditions or the essential and fundamental elements of cooperation; a variable component of up to 60% maximum to reward performance towards the mdgs and linked to result indicators mainly in the areas of health and education and progress in public financial management. eligible countries are those that have already implemented budget support satisfactorily under the 9th edf, but also those that continue to demonstrate a strong commitment to monitoring and achieving the mdgs, to improving the management of budgetary resources of countries where there is proper coordination between donors. after assessing 10 countries, the commission has designed mdg contracts in seven of them: burkina faso, ghana, mali, mozambique, rwanda, uganda, tanzania and zambia. these programmes were submitted and approved by the member states last december. three contracts have already been signed: zambia and rwanda which i have personally signed, and mali, and the others will be finalised in the very next few weeks. collectively, these seven programmes represent around eur 1.8 billion, or some 50% of total general budget support, and some 14% of total national indicative programmes of the 10th edf. of course, we will seek, as your report encourages us to do, to extend this mechanism to other countries, including non-acp countries, on the basis of the experience we will gain from these first countries. obviously, alternative approaches will have to be devised for countries not yet eligible for budget support, but the mdg contract is already making an important contribution to improving aid effectiveness and accelerating progress towards the achievement of the millennium development goals.
the presentation is closed. the vote will take place on tuesday 24 march 2009. the commission shall be assisted by the committee of the regions.
the agenda includes the report by mr lasse lehtinen, on behalf of the committee on employment and social affairs, on the social responsibility of subcontracting companies in production chains [2008/2249 ((ini)) ] (a6-0065/2009).
member of the commission. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the commission welcomes this report very much. however important subcontracting may be for increasing productivity and competitiveness, we fully recognise the need for effective measures to ensure that subcontracting does not encourage or facilitate non-compliance with terms and conditions of employment, particularly in the case of long subcontracting chains. adequate, effective and dissuasive penalties are necessary to ensure that subcontractors fully comply with their legal or contractual obligations, in particular with regard to workers' rights. greater transparency in subcontracting processes will lead to better protection of workers' rights in general, which is something the commission is and remains very committed to, as you know. while i agree with your general principle that european problems require a european response, i would be more cautious about the conclusion in paragraph 14 of the report that the problem can only be solved by a clear legal instrument which introduces joint and joint responsibility at european level. the report also seems to go in this direction in paragraph 15, where it calls for an impact analysis on the added value and feasibility of such a community instrument. as regards the call to the commission in paragraph 25 to ensure effective compliance with the directive on the posting of workers, i would like to point out that we have recently set up a high-level group of experts on the posting of workers. this group of experts, composed of representatives of the member states and the social partners, aims to improve the practical application of the directive and in particular administrative cooperation between the member states. it will hold its first meeting on 25 march. in this respect, i would like to point out that a study entitled 'liability in subcontracting processes in the european construction sector', published in 2008 by the european foundation for the improvement of living and working conditions, clearly shows significant differences between national systems of joint and several liability, as well as in their effectiveness. the study also highlighted the fact that there does not appear to be a one-size-fits-all solution and recommended further debate and research, particularly on cross-border aspects. the problem we are trying to solve is social, but the proposed solution clearly has implications that go far beyond the social realm. the economic and legal implications of this should therefore be studied in detail. i fully agree that this problem deserves further research and that we must carefully consider various non-regulatory methods of dealing with a number of the aspects raised in the report before we put forward a legislative proposal, namely: better cooperation and coordination between national authorities, inspections and other national law enforcement authorities, awareness of companies about good practice, existing guidelines and standards, social responsibility initiatives and transnational corporate agreements which already contain innovative provisions on risk assessment procedures and the supervision of subcontractors.
the presentation is closed. the vote will take place on thursday 26 march 2009. the commission shall be assisted by the committee of the regions.

initiatives and dialogues we have established with india. we believe it is of the utmost importance to successfully negotiate and conclude an ambitious free trade agreement with india that will result in a win-win scenario for both parties, the european union and india. the more ambitious the free trade agreement, the greater the economic benefits that can be realised by both parties, the european union and india. this is one of the main conclusions of the impact and sustainable development study carried out by an independent consultant in parallel with the negotiations. the objective of the impact and sustainable development study was to analyse the economic, social and environmental impact of the future free trade agreement and to identify possible necessary accompanying measures. the impact and sustainability study is currently in its final phase and should be available in april, therefore well in time to support the ongoing negotiations. let me briefly inform you of the state of progress of these negotiations. six negotiating sessions have been held since the launch in june 2007, the sixth session was held last week in delhi from 17 to 19 march. we expect to agree on two more sessions this year, ideally after the indian elections in april and before the eu/india summit in november. as regards the substance of these negotiations, progress has been made on all the subjects covered by the free trade agreement, but there is still much work to be done. more concretely, we exchanged tariff offers, had good discussions on a few key service sectors and made progress on text discussions in almost all areas of the agreement. however, we are still far from an agreement. before concluding, i would like to express once again the commission's gratitude to parliament and to the rapporteur. the commission looks forward to further opportunities to cooperate effectively with parliament.
the presentation is closed. the vote will take place on thursday 26 march 2009. the commission shall be assisted by the committee of the regions.
the agenda includes the report by katerina batzeli, on behalf of the committee on agriculture and rural development, on food prices in europe [2008/2175(ini) ] (a6-0094/2009).
member of the commission. - i would first like to thank mrs batzeli and the members of the agri committee for drawing up this report, which is being debated with great difficulty at a crucial moment for the agri-food chain in the european union. as you all know, the recession has led to a sharp downturn in activity in most economic sectors in the european union. the agricultural sector is experiencing a real collapse in market prices which is seriously affecting farm incomes. the situation is particularly serious in high value-added sectors such as meat and dairy products. in this context, it is vital that the agri-food chain functions efficiently if the effects of the crisis on farm incomes are to be mitigated and consumers are to benefit from food products at lower prices. the agri-food chain and the question of food prices therefore remain the commission's main concerns. the analysis of structural factors raises fears of a further rise in the prices of agricultural raw materials in the medium and long term. by improving the functioning of the agri-food chain, it should be possible to avoid similar sharp increases in food prices in the future and to contain the volatility of consumer prices. i share most of the concerns expressed in the report about the need to improve the overall functioning of the agri-food chain. in particular, this will increase transparency across the supply chain, provide consumers with better information and improve the distribution of added value across the entire supply chain. since last year, the commission has taken a series of initiatives to improve the functioning of the agri-food chain. the high level group on the competitiveness of the agri-food industry has recently issued a set of strategic recommendations. a green paper on the quality of agricultural products was also presented last year. in the communication on food prices adopted last december, the commission also proposed, in the form of a roadmap, a number of formulas to improve the functioning of the agri-food chain in europe. it is absolutely vital that we move forward with the implementation of this roadmap. we must make progress in particular in setting up a permanent european observatory of the agri-food chain and food prices. by providing reliable information on prices across the supply chain, we can help to combat the lack of transparency and improve our knowledge of how the supply chain works. we must also go further in analysing the distribution of value added across the whole sector. this is a point to which i attach particular importance. as acknowledged in the food price communication, the asymmetry of bargaining power between agricultural producers and the rest of the industry weighs heavily on the margins of producers in the agricultural sector. it is clear that an effort to clarify and understand the question of the distribution of value added would be a first step towards rebalancing the bargaining power throughout the industry. it should be stressed in this connection that the competitiveness of the agri-food chain in the european union cannot be built at the expense of some of its components. it is essential that the agri-food industry and retailers can continue to rely on a sustainable and competitive agricultural production platform within the european union. i am convinced that once fully implemented, the road map proposed by the commission will enable us to respond to most of the questions and concerns raised in mrs batzeli's report.
the presentation is closed. the vote will take place on thursday 26 march 2009. the commission shall be assisted by the committee of the regions.

education, and innovation encourages the creation of synergies between traditional and more innovative fields of activity. today, we need to combine technology and design, integrating the principles skills, which are of great use in professional life. the european agenda for culture has introduced new methods, including structured dialogue with civil society and, more recently, new open methods from my colleague, mr figel.

the agenda includes the report by mrs cristiana muscardini, on behalf of the committee on women's rights and gender equality, on combating female genital mutilation in the eu [2008/2071(ini) ] (a6-0054/2009).
the rapporteur. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i think it is particularly appropriate that commissioner michel, who we know is always very attentive to human rights problems and the tragedies that are developing in africa, should take part in this debate. and it is precisely the presence of commissioner michel that gives me hope that the commission can be particularly attentive to a problem which today is no longer limited to the 28 african countries and several countries in the middle east and also neighbouring countries, it is a problem which is particularly acute today within the european union itself. the great immigration that has taken place in recent years has brought this tragedy to the countries of the european union as well. every day tens of thousands of girls and teenagers are at risk of a horrific practice that will permanently damage them physically, but also severely damage them mentally. that is why - after parliament had already spoken out on other occasions in previous years and had even given, through dafne, funding to 14 projects to combat female sexual handicaps - that is why we are again dealing with this issue today, because unfortunately the phenomenon has not regressed, it has not diminished, but is still expanding. we must have the courage to use a more appropriate and serious prevention through cultural campaigns that give immigrant women, but also the fathers of these girls, the knowledge that it is not by following a tribal ritual, that it has nothing to do with religion, that neither integration nor a future for their daughters can be achieved. let us think of a girl who goes to school in france, italy or belgium and who, after socializing with her peers, is suddenly torn from her normal life and forced to suffer a tragedy that marks her for the rest of her life. this child will not only be physically handicapped, but will be unable to relate properly to other people, will feel diminished, different and we do not want different in this society. we want people who, regardless of religion, colour or geographical origin, can work together to build a better europe that is closer to its citizens. that is why, mr president and commissioner, we as a parliament - and i would like to thank all the ladies in the committee who helped me to draw up this report - want the laws of all the countries in europe to be harmonized so that sexual harassment of women is identified as a crime. we also do not want palliative measures such as the so-called "puncture" to be proposed. we want women to be truly equal to men, that there be no initiation rites, but that there be true integration. we want the ngos to be able to work, we want prevention to involve the associations of immigrant women, we want to punish anyone who wants to maim the girls and drag them into a perverse spiral of despair and marginalisation. there are many points in the report which i think our colleagues have had a chance to examine and evaluate. i believe that an appeal to the strong will of a europe which brings together its three institutions to combat this horrible crime which violates human rights must be the aim of everyone.
member of the commission. - mr president, i would like to thank mrs muscardini, not only on behalf of my colleague but also on my own behalf, for her speech, because i think she is pointing to a drama is a sign of a lack of acceptance in our countries to say: 'this is our constitution, these are our rules, these are our human values, you must respect them. if you do not, you are breaking the law and must be punished". i'm closing the parenthesis, but it felt good to say it because i totally share your irritation about this subject. in its external aid to third countries, the commission also awareness-raising activities for all sectors of society. the hague multiannual programme, which covers the various actions to be carried out in order to develop the area of justice, freedom and external policies.

in writing. o i support the report by mr alain hutchinson and fully support the call on the commission to continue to link its aid in the areas of health and education, in particular basic health and primary education, to the results achieved in these areas and to improve the predictability of financial aid through the implementation of mdg contracts. they also agree on the importance of being able to extend the principles deriving from these contracts to a greater number of countries, as the mdg contract has as its main objective to contribute to improving the effectiveness of aid and accelerating progress towards the mdgs for the countries that need them most. i believe it is of the utmost importance that the commission makes its financial aid conditional on achievements in the field of good governance and transparency, but also on the defence and respect of human rights, in particular those of the poorest and the most marginalized such as the disabled, minorities, women and children, and to ensure that financial aid is not spent in areas other than those defined in the mdg agreement.
in writing. - i wish to abstain on the report by mr hutchinson on contracts relating to the millennium development goals: i agree with some of the points raised and cannot therefore give my full approval to the text.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, my vote is in favour. "all children are born artists. the challenge is to remain so as you grow up". with these words pablo picasso described the difficulties of artistic training. at present, although it is a compulsory subject in many school systems, art education continues to be taught according to learning models which vary considerably from one member state to another. the development of new information and communication technologies has stimulated a knowledge-based economy, allowing intellectual capacity and creativity to play a leading role. in this context, arts education plays an important role in preserving identity and promoting intercultural and interreligious understanding. art education is also the tool for developing the human resources needed to exploit the rich cultural heritage of a country. in addition, there is a growing need for competitiveness in many areas, with various school systems now giving priority to the development of creativity through educational programmes based on appropriate pedagogical methods and able to ensure that pupils have a significant potential for later entry into the world of work.
in writing. - i welcome the report by mrs badia i cutchet on art studies in the european union. i believe that at the present time, when our societies are becoming more and more heterogeneous, culture is of fundamental importance as a means of preserving identities and at the same time improving the coexistence between different peoples and cultures. i agree that art is a manifestation of culture and allows to develop both the cultural wealth of a country and society in general: the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos at work. in view of the importance of the arts, i am therefore in favour of coordination at european level of their teaching in schools.
in writing. - i wish to abstain on the report by mr hegyi on active dialogue with citizens on europe. in fact, while i agree with some of the text presented, i do not agree with several points which i consider important: i therefore cannot give my full support to the report.
in writing. - i express my negative opinion on the report by mr cornillet on the activities of the acp-eu joint parliamentary assembly in 2008. i think that the work done in the working sessions so far has not always been satisfactory, and that on some important subjects no resolution has been adopted. in addition, the negotiations undertaken by the assembly have in some cases led to the conclusion of partnership agreements which have not produced good results for either the european union or the counterparts. i therefore express my negative opinion of the report.
in writing. - i vote against the report by mrs krehl on best practice in regional policy and obstacles to the use of the structural funds. i am convinced that the proposals in this report do not represent a chance to improve the functioning of regional policy, which is a very important policy to combat unbalanced development within the european union and which enjoys strong financial support. i believe, in particular, that the exchange of good practice cannot be the solution to the problem of the most efficient use of structural resources and that it cannot really contribute to the development of innovative projects.
in writing. - i am voting against the report by mr roszkowski on the complementarity and coordination of cohesion policy and rural development measures. i doubt, in particular, that support for non-agricultural activities in rural regions is the most effective way of strengthening territorial cohesion. i think that this is a threat to direct aid to agriculture, and that it is causing serious imbalances in the socioeconomic situation of rural areas.
in writing. i am voting in favour of the report by mrs roth-behrendt on the proposal for a european parliament and council regulation on cosmetic products. i fully agree that in order to increase the safety of cosmetic products, in order to ensure the protection and health of all consumers, specific control instruments must be clearly defined. i also agree with the honourable member that in order to strengthen the control mechanism so as to ensure independent evaluation, the responsibility for declarations concerning cosmetic products should be entrusted to an independent organisation.
in writing. - i give my vote in favour of the report by mrs sârbu on the proposal for a european parliament and council directive amending directive 98/8/ec concerning the placing of biocidal products on the market as regards the extension of certain time periods. given the delicate and laborious process of evaluating active substances used in biocidal products, i agree with the rapporteur that the transitional period should be extended to four years instead of three, in order to give the industry the time it needs to fulfil its tasks.
in writing. i am voting against the report by mr becsey on the proposal for a council directive amending directives 92/79/eec, 92/80/eec and 95/59/ec as regards the structure and rates of excise duty on manufactured tobacco. i do not approve of this proposal because i think it would weaken the commission's proposal. as a result, the achievement of the planned targets of contributing to the reduction of tobacco consumption by 10% by 2014 would be hampered.
in writing. - my vote is in favour. a wild and illegal practice, practised mainly in africa, has been quietly introduced into europe through immigration to the old continent over the last thirty years. the who data is clear: female genital mutilation (fgm) is widespread in 28 african countries, the middle east and some asian countries. some 100 to 140 million women and girls worldwide have been subjected to the practice, while 4 million are potentially at risk. fgm is a handicap to the process of european integration, as well as a denigration of gender equality. the european parliament, which has been committed for years to affirming the fundamental rights of all citizens, had already adopted a resolution on the subject in 2001, but it is time to take a step forward by also supporting the dafne iii programme which has so far funded 14 projects on fgm, outlining priorities for the prevention and elimination of fgm in europe. one of the areas where action needs to be stepped up is the prevention of this practice against girls, and to this end, intervention that can identify children at risk is crucial, making prevention with families through psychological support.
in writing. - i am voting in favour of the report by mrs muscardini on the fight against female genital mutilation in the eu. i consider these practices to be egregious violations of the human right to privacy. i therefore agree with the rapporteur that a sound strategy should be put in place to prevent and eliminate fgm.
in writing. - i have spoken out in favour of multilingualism on several occasions, and i think my position is quite clear. the linguistic and cultural diversity of the european union is a huge competitive advantage. i believe it is essential to promote programmes for language teaching and cultural and student exchange both within and outside the community, as i did when i supported the erasmus mundus programme. multilingualism is essential for effective communication and is a tool to facilitate understanding between people and, consequently, the acceptance of differences and minorities. linguistic diversity, as a consequence of media penetration, increasing mobility, migration and the advance of cultural globalisation, also affects important aspects of the daily lives of the citizens of the european union. the acquisition of a diverse range of language skills is crucial for all eu citizens, as it enables them to take full advantage of the economic, social and cultural benefits of free movement within the union and in its relations with third countries. language is a key factor in social inclusion. europe's linguistic diversity is therefore a fundamental cultural asset and it would be wrong for the european union to limit itself to one main language.
in writing. - i support the report by mr moura on multilingualism as a resource for europe and a common commitment. in particular, as a university professor, i strongly support the proposal to promote programmes for language teaching and cultural and student exchange, such as the well-known youth mobility programmes. these projects, managed by the commission's education and culture dg, enable students to significantly increase their educational background, thus contributing to the eu's journey towards a knowledge-based society.
in writing. - i am voting against the report by mr van nistelrooij on territorial cohesion and the state of play of the debate on the future reform of cohesion policy on the green paper on territorial cohesion and the state of play of the debate on the future. the reasons for my disagreement stem from a different view of territorial cohesion, and i do not feel that i agree with the rapporteur's views.
in writing. - i am voting against the report by mr vlasák on the urban dimension of cohesion policy in the new programming period. while i understand the importance of sustainable urban development, i believe it is difficult to achieve this without a common definition of 'urban areas'.

on behalf of the uen group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the car crisis is one of the most serious in the world manufacturing industry because, in addition to having serious economic and employment repercussions on european factories and industry, it affects non-community countries where production has been increasingly displaced in recent decades. the union cannot bear the social cost of cutting some 350 000 jobs in order to restore the sector to at least its 2007 level of profitability. i would therefore welcome at least harmonised aid to the sector, provided that it is combined with the safeguarding of employment. the keywords for european enterprises must be research and advanced technology. it is obvious that in the evolution of the market the use of mergers or strategic agreements is another possible way forward, but this is not at the expense of the european tradition of the car, the flagship of the community manufacturing industry.
i am sorry to say that the commission has not been able to reach a decision on the matter. we are discussing this when certain choices have already been made by national governments outside a genuine european context, and the social consequences are already dramatic in terms of unemployment and social integration. the text of the resolution does not contain any essential elements for the measures to be taken to be effective and fair. i would point out that europe, as a real political actor, had acted very differently on climate a few months ago. that is not happening in the economic crisis. it has been left to governments who have acted in a disconnected way and, i would say, with some electoral logic. this is of course due to the political weakness of the barroso commission, but also to the difficulties in dealing with situations which require a new capacity for intervention with choices concerning industrial, social and employment policies. can we expect nationalistic measures? can a wave of redundancies be expected in the presence of aid to enterprises? can we continue to have relocations in the car and related sectors, as in the italian case of itono and now with the indesit case, which concerns another key sector? can the use of european funds be expanded without increasing them? so it's not enough to say there's a car problem and that there's been a lot of meetings. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. my group has tabled amendments to all these. we need a new policy, one that europe has not shown to have and which we must implement before the social disadvantage becomes so dramatic that we cannot build certain answers for our workers.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i wanted to speak on this subject because in recent months i have followed very closely the work that has been carried out in the european parliament, in our committees and then in the house, concerning precisely the specific commitments that we have asked of the car manufacturers of our continent. we set important targets, particularly on co2, when we asked them to participate in the major targets that europe has set for co2 reduction in the coming years, ambitious targets that all countries in the world are looking at with great interest. we have asked the automotive industry to have an average reduction of 120 mg by 2012 and another 25 mg by 2020. these are important objectives that require significant investment. i would add to this the fact, already mentioned by some of my colleagues, that the automobile sector directly and indirectly employs 12 million workers in europe, or 6% of employment in europe. if europe is serious about giving its car industry the means to achieve the co2 targets we have set and if we want to defend jobs which are a problem for our continent at the moment, we need a coordinated strategy to help this sector. several member states are launching plans to encourage sales, which is in line with maintaining fleet renewal levels. however, these policies must be part of a single community strategy to avoid dangerous market distortions.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, this is the third debate we have had on the car in a few months. our requests have not yet been adequately answered by the commission and the council, either in terms of supporting demand or in terms of external competition with adequate export support. while i believe that european action to deal with the financial crisis is significant, i believe that, contrary to the conclusions of the recent summit, the european response to the recession and the difficulties of the real economy is insufficient. we are at war and our soldiers, who are our enterprises, have their weapons loaded to the hilt. the automobile sector is a fundamental sector of our industry, subject to new needs, reorganization of production factors and strong innovative process and product requirements. coordinated european scrapping incentives against all protectionism, refinancing of credit lines by the european bank for investment in this sector, incentives only for eco-friendly cars and hybrid engines, more research funds for clean engines and strong action within the world trade organisation to create conditions of genuine reciprocity in the world car market are the most significant demands of those who do not want to promote the deindustrialization of europe in one of its crucial sectors with high added value and employment.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner verheugen has stressed the need to be very careful that protectionist measures are not proposed or supported. i would remind him that across the atlantic these measures are being taken and obviously favour the competitors of european producers. i have the impression that the strategy pursued by the european union so far is not sufficiently focused, as it should be in a critical situation such as the present one, on supporting exclusively or mainly the 'european' car, designed and built here in europe. i have heard from trade unionists crocodile tears about deindustrialization, relocation and so on. when someone like myself, at the assembly of even a large italian car manufacturer, made these claims years ago, they were not taken very seriously. today, unfortunately, the facts are right. if europe limits itself to measures designed to stimulate demand, which can of course also be directed at non-european producers, it will not achieve the results that are needed, and to achieve them it is urgent to stimulate the production of european cars. european manufacturers must be encouraged to invest in research to ensure the future of an excellent industrial sector, including the car industry, which is also suffering today from a policy of financial restraint by european banking institutions.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i should like to begin by expressing my appreciation for the timely commitment of the commission and the council to support the car industry and the manufacturers of motor vehicles and their components, which is not yet sufficient. after the first measures taken by the member states, the sector has recovered slightly: the italian figure shows a -18% fall in sales in february, compared with a 22% fall in january. of course, given the data mentioned by commissioner verheugen himself, europe must go further by providing additional eib financing and increasingly coordinating national measures to avoid unfair and discriminatory competition. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to carcinogens at work. in the light of the dramatic figures on redundancies and the measures to integrate the cash-flow, i ask the commission to make more decisive proposals on the better use of the social fund and the globalisation adjustment fund.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the car industry is one of the key sectors of the european economy and one which is very much at risk in the current crisis. this is not the time to say that we must be against protectionism and unfair competition. all of this is terribly obvious. the time has come to give european producers and workers clear and bold strategic assurances, with a support plan, i stress, which gives all member states the same opportunities. the objectives certainly include ensuring better use of european funds, including the globalisation fund, but above all simplifying and increasing financial support to the sector through the eib and the ecb to access low-interest loans, also simplifying administrative procedures. i would conclude by saying that more generally the aim is to maintain the competitiveness of the sector and to ensure that all the initiatives at european level, in addition to addressing the current emergency, can help to open a positive phase of restructuring and transformation of the automotive industry.
