in writing. - i support the marinescu report because the eu's enlargement policy, accompanied by an active neighbourhood policy, has extended the european aviation market to 37 countries. with the extension of the single air transport market, the eu is now a global player. the single european sky (ses) initiative was launched in 2000 and brought atm into the common transport policy. the competitiveness of the european air transport industry requires a comprehensive system approach with a common vision, objectives and technologies, based on a sound regulatory framework. in this respect, the commission has put forward a package of proposals, but some of the elements can be improved, such as ensuring the functional independence of the national supervisory authorities and also greater involvement of all parties. to do this, cooperation at political, social and technical levels is essential if the aim of the ceu is to be achieved. like the rapporteur, i believe that the commission should first of all work towards defining quantifiable and achievable community objectives focused on the need to address all sensitive areas such as safety, the environment, capacity and cost-effectiveness.
in writing. - i support the report by mr marinescu on the performance and sustainability of the european aviation system. i share the views of the honourable member on the need for a revision of the legislative framework for the single european sky (ses) initiative, since since 2000, when it was launched, the expected results do not seem to have been achieved, in particular in terms of increased flight efficiency, cost reduction and the elimination of the fragmentation and general inefficiencies of the air transport system that still persist. these inefficiencies unfortunately translate into high costs in terms of expenses, time and fuel waste for those who benefit from the single european sky. i also believe that it is necessary to push for the revision of the legislation in line with the commission's proposals, in order to ensure, among other things, the independence of the national supervisory authorities, the harmonisation of safety requirements, a single european airborne information region, without neglecting the greater involvement of the social partners in the system approach, because i believe that only with a broad consensus at the grassroots level can the current technical and political obstacles be overcome and the ambitious objectives of the initiative be achieved.
in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i support mr marinescu's report on airports, air traffic management and air navigation services because it is part of the wider framework of the single european sky initiative, on which i have already expressed my favourable opinion. i agree with my colleague that to meet the future challenges in the aviation market, especially in the field of aviation safety, it is necessary to introduce a system of harmonised standards at european level. there are still many differences between the national safety procedures which should be eliminated in the light of the commission's proposals, in particular those concerning the responsibilities of the european aviation safety agency, which is certainly an important instrument for improving the safety of air transport in europe. i think it is necessary, however, to stress, as the honourable member has done, the need to ensure the proportionality of the measures, safeguarding the use of local knowledge and expertise and also ensuring cooperation between aesa and eurocontrol, in order to avoid red tape and inefficient duplication of tasks and responsibilities.
in writing. - i support the commission's proposal to amend regulation (ec) no 258/97 on novel foods and novel food ingredients in order to make the necessary simplifications and centralising the authorisation and placing on the market of novel foods. the introduction of the new regulation would protect consumers by introducing a high level of food safety, environmental protection and animal health protection, taking into account at all times the precautionary principle as laid down in regulation (ec) no 178/2002 of the european parliament and of the council of 28 january 2002. that regulation lays down the general principles and requirements of food law, establishes the european food safety authority and lays down procedures in the field of food safety. the commission proposal seeks to make the authorisation procedure more efficient and transparent and to improve its implementation. this will help to improve the application of the regulation and will give consumers greater powers and choice as they will be able to have more information.
in writing. i am voting in favour of the proposal by mrs liotard on novel foods. i agree with your colleague that a high level of food safety, consumer protection, environmental protection and animal health must be achieved, always taking the precautionary principle into account. i also believe that it is essential that new foodstuffs should not endanger the lives of consumers or mislead them, because the health and safety of citizens would be dangerously compromised.
in writing. - if the montreal protocol, which entered into force 20 years ago and has been signed by 193 nations, had not banned products that contribute to the reduction of the ozone hole, a catastrophic scenario would have been foreseen for planet earth. the main culprits for the loss of atmospheric ozone are halogenated hydrocarbons, chemicals invented in 1928 as refrigerants. when the ozone hole was first detected in the 1980's, researchers discovered that these chemicals, which are practically inactive at the earth's surface, are able to interact with ozone molecules in the atmosphere and destroy the protective shield against harmful uv rays. to remedy this situation, the montreal protocol was signed in 1987 and will enter into force two years later. one thing is certain, we have done everything we can to make our air unbreathable. progress has played an important role in this phase, providing us with a range of services and goods that over the past few decades have contributed to a progressive deterioration in the conditions of our climate system. the greenhouse effect, the ozone hole and climate change are just some of the phenomena which must be the focus of our attention as representatives of our fellow citizens and future children in europe. that's why i'm in favor.
in writing. - i shall vote in favour of the report by mr blokland on substances that deplete the ozone layer. i share the aims of the project, which are to protect the stratospheric ozone layer and prevent climate change, as banned substances have not only a significant ozone depleting potential (odp), but also a global warming potential (gwp). i also agree with the amendments tabled, which seek to improve the regulation further in the light of the problems, so that the eu can set itself more ambitious objectives and take a leading role in the world.
in writing. - i shall abstain on the report by mr virrankoski on the abb-abm method as a management tool for the allocation of budgetary resources. i fully agree with the honourable member that there is an absolute need for clarity on the results achieved and the resources needed to achieve them and that citizens should be fully informed about the cost of european union policies. i am not sure, however, that the system in question can solve the problem, and i shall therefore abstain from voting for or against it.
in writing. - i vote in favour. the institutional future of the european union was given a new impetus by the european council of june 2007. the 27 member states have decided to convene an intergovernmental conference to prepare the new treaty on the basis of the draft constitution. if the ratification procedures proceed as expected, the new treaty could enter into force in mid-2009, roughly coinciding with the european elections. if the ratification process were to be held up, it would have unforeseeable consequences for the european project. the revision process must therefore take account of this new context. if the timetable set out in the european council conclusions is respected, the entry into force of the new treaty, the election of the new parliament (june 2009) and the appointment of the new commission should take place in the second half of 2009. in such a situation, the interinstitutional debate on the revision could be postponed to avoid any risk of confusion. i think that this parliament has made a considerable investment with the work of its temporary committee on political challenges and budgetary resources as well as with the annual budgets and the legislative work that has followed. the ini report, therefore, as a legacy of the outgoing parliament, should reflect the successes achieved so far, but also highlight the shortcomings that still exist.

in writing. - i give my vote in favour of the motion for a resolution on the interim economic partnership agreement between the ec and côte d'ivoire. i agree that a customs union between the west african countries could be a great benefit to the ivory coast, which is the trade and economic leader of that area: in addition, in view of the fact that intra-regional trade represents only a small part of the total trade of côte d'ivoire, it is appropriate to increase regional trade links in order to develop sustained and sustainable growth in the long term. it is also desirable that the european union should provide greater and better technical and administrative assistance to côte d'ivoire to ensure that its economy is able to fully absorb the benefits of the interim economic partnership agreement.

extraordinary care. article 13 of the treaty is clear. it is a solid legal basis and a directive based on that legal basis is not in conflict with the principle of subsidiarity. another essential principle of this directive is the question of, for example, the transfer of the burden of proof. this issue has already been addressed in previous directives, so that this is not a breakthrough the rapporteur. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i should like to begin by thanking all those who have worked so effectively on this report: the european parliament has been very active in this area, and i would like to thank the rapporteur, mr pimenta, for his excellent report. their valuable cooperation made the agreement at first reading possible. by taking over responsibility for the review of the ecolabel dossier on behalf of the european parliament, i have moved in the direction of giving a boost to this system which, through the constant updating of the environmental requirements for the products that bear it, encourages companies to make a continuous virtuous effort to raise the overall ecological quality standards of the products placed on the market. by increasing the production and distribution of ecolabelled products and services, we will achieve significant, permanent and growing environmental benefits in the coming years in terms of energy savings, reduction of air pollution and water savings. the ecolabel is a voluntary eco-label intended to promote the dissemination of products and services with a reduced environmental impact throughout their life cycle by providing consumers with accurate, non-misleading and scientifically correct information. the revision of this regulation is part of the wider european action plan for sustainable consumption and production and is closely linked to the revision of emas and the ecodesign directive. the revision of the regulation had already been provided for by the community legislature: the system must be reviewed in the light of experience and modified to increase its effectiveness, improve planning and simplify operation. the aim of the label is to guide consumers towards products that reduce their environmental impact. to date, the ecolabel experience has been mixed: on the one hand, an increasing number of companies are seeking quality certification in a wide range of sectors, thus recognising its selective and driving value. this certification is highly appreciated by consumers who are more concerned with the social responsibility of enterprises. on the other hand, a number of problems should be noted: the lack of awareness of the trade mark among the general public; the rapid obsolescence of criteria in relation to market developments; the bureaucratic delays that slow down the participation of operators. the new ecolabel brand will take on a new look, not only in terms of graphics but also in terms of content. it will become more attractive, its scope will be extended to new products: we expect to double the number of groups from the current 25 to 40-50 by 2015. promotion campaigns were planned; a marketing budget of eur 9.5 million has been implemented and a website will be made for which eur 15 000 is planned. the principle that most interested the shadow rapporteurs and was agreed by the other institutions was that the ecolabel should not just be a certification of an achievement but rather a dynamic tool in continuous evolution, a springboard that constantly pushes manufacturers and products towards higher environmental quality standards, continuously assessing excellence in the market and setting new criteria accordingly. what we want to ensure is a control of the entire life cycle of the product, which allows the maximum consideration of the environmental impact at all stages of production and allows all operators in the sector, as well as ngos, to participate actively in the process of reviewing the criteria for compromise. the rapporteur. - i accept your invitation.
i would like to thank the rapporteur for his excellent report. eco-labelling is sustainable, but it is also environmentally friendly: this is the challenge of the new framework regulation on the ecolabel. the regulation is a first step. the european parliament and the council have had fruitful and constructive negotiations, at least on the chemicals side. it is now up to the commission to develop the criteria, implement a work plan and draw up a first list of products within one year. the individual member states must organise the national competent authority, liaise with the european body and adopt the sustainability criteria as binding. but what is environmental sustainability for the ecolabel? it means applying innovative production criteria to the entire product lifecycle, from reducing emissions in production techniques, to reducing the energy consumption of primary goods such as water, to locating production close to the final consumer, which is a real revolution. this is the challenge that we face in a coherent fight against climate change but also in a genuine innovation of the way we produce. in developing these criteria, the commission and the new community body are invited to involve the active players and best practices actively, drawing on the innovations they have experienced in their production cycles, thus making them accessible and transparent. the respect of social standards at work is an integral part of these criteria, even if the regulation still maintains, because of incomprehensible pressure from the council in the final negotiations, a legally unacceptable deadline. it's called "if necessary". the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament on the subject of the social clauses. the exclusions for products that contain toxic chemicals, substances harmful to the environment, carcinogens or substances harmful to reproduction are clear and effective. warning: the european parliament's control over this will be particularly rigid.

the rapporteur. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i thank the czech presidency, the commission, the chairman of the committee on energy and industry, mr niebler, and the other rapporteurs on this energy package, the shadow rapporteurs, the committee secretariat and all its officials for the cooperation and expertise shown in this dossier. we can and should all be proud of the result achieved; i am, thinking of the effort i made when i inherited the directive on the internal gas market, with problems that are not easily solved. i am glad that i have made this, my second experience as a member of the european parliament, coincide with the final phase of this package, which i consider to be one of the most important dossiers of this legislature, for the benefit of the european citizens who are our electors. the gas directive, which will come into force in 2011, brings significant new developments in the sector: the achievement of the ito option, which guarantees the opening up of markets and real progress towards a system which really allows the european union to speak with one voice on energy, must be emphasized as an important result. litit is the real novelty of this package and it is the one on which the european parliament has arguably had the best result. the new gas directive gives a lot of importance to the gas authorities and the agency. this directive legitimises the authorities in their role, particularly in those countries where they have to start their activities from scratch. it is therefore of fundamental importance that the role and powers of these bodies have been defined and that they have been given broad powers, since the authorities have the difficult task of monitoring the common energy market. another element, which was inserted during the trilogue phase, is the exemption from the common rules of the so-called closed systems, i.e. airports, hospitals, stations, industrial sites, etc., which, due to their particular characteristics, are subject to a more favourable regime, as a demonstration of the attention that the new directive pays to the needs of the european citizen. i believe that the european citizen is the one who will really benefit from this directive, because by using smart meters he will have access to all the information on the bill and will be able to evaluate the best offer on the market and choose his supplier according to convenience, because although it is true that it will take years to see the effects of this liberalisation, it is undeniable that the entry of new players on the market will lead to lower prices and more favourable market conditions for the citizens of the union. another important element is the recognition of european transmission system systems which will ensure the security of gas supply to european citizens. this also means strengthening and creating new infrastructure such as regasifiers and storage facilities which will be the driving force behind the third package. the opening up of a competitive market that guarantees long-term investment and contracts by companies in the sector is therefore required, particularly in the new member states where the creation of new infrastructure would also make it possible to solve problems of age-old dependence. the weakest consumer has been protected by allowing the national and regional authorities to guarantee gas supplies at the most critical moments. the successful outcome of the gas directive of the whole energy package once again highlights the role of europe and its institutions for the european citizens.
mr stolojan, since you have been so present in this debate, even though i told you that you exceeded the number, i think that your responsibility and your presence should be rewarded, so i shall exceptionally give you the floor for a minute.
the rapporteur. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, this joint debate has produced a very strong feeling: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. it will not be the last, because, as you know, there is a great push to use other sources of energy, renewable and nuclear, but it will certainly help to satisfy hunger and the need for energy in the next 10 to 15 to 20 years and to anticipate and, of course, protect consumers, especially the most vulnerable. i believe that mr morgan, the undersigned and all the other honourable members, have played a very important role in defending the weak consumer, giving a great deal of power to the national and regional authorities, who can, at critical moments, change, i do not say give free energy, but certainly change and allow a continuous supply of this energy. the other key point is this: i would like to say that the commission is very pleased that the council has taken the initiative to adopt this package, which is essential for energy consumers. i think there is nothing more serious than not letting people know who is benefiting from a great work without informing them. i think that the task which will fall to the commission, the council and parliament, before they even bother to apply this package, is to let consumers know that this package exists, what has been done for them, in their capacity and for them again.

in writing. - my vote is in favour. the european commission has always been extremely careful to guarantee the individual rights of mobile citizens, especially as regards those benefits relating to social security. the free movement of citizens within the eu's borders is one of the fundamental freedoms of the citizen and it promotes the development of the internal economy of our member states. that is why the commission wants to step up its efforts to ensure that eu citizens and their families actually enjoy the rights guaranteed by existing european legislation. although in some areas national legislation provides community citizens and their families with better treatment than that provided for in current european legislation, no member state has ratified all the directives issued in this field in a completely correct manner. the violation of the fundamental rights of eu citizens in the exercise of the right of free movement within the european territory, which is often continuous, is particularly evident in relation to the following phenomena: the right of entry and residence of family members who are third-country nationals; the lack of assistance for work-related accidents. we hope that the commission will continue its technical cooperation with the member states, which has already identified a number of issues for further discussion and clarification, particularly with regard to abuses.
in writing. - my vote is in favour. one of the most debated points in the policies discussed by the european union is the implementation of a common policy for the protection of individuals. the concept of personality is certainly very broad, but today a common definition has been reached, meaning all those individuals who hold an official or unofficial position and who may be threatened because of their contributions to the public debate. the incidents involving former member of the dutch parliament, hirshi ali, who was threatened in february 2008 after her valuable speech on the extremely topical issue of islamic radicalisation in europe, and the famous anglo-indian writer samal rushdie, persecuted because of his controversial views on the islamic religion, were well known. it is therefore desirable that every person who is concerned with the positive development of public debate should have the right to be protected when visiting a state where he might be threatened or attacked, especially as in the case of samal rushdie, where the death sentence has already been pronounced against him by a third state.
in writing. - my vote is in favour. the alpine region is one of the most important and richest territories within the european community. it has eight neighbouring states which have signed joint agreements on the protection and conservation of this region and a common transport management policy since 4 april 1998. in the transport sector, the so-called 'protocol on the implementation of the alpine convention in the field of transport' was adopted on 24-26 may 2000 and its main task was to provide a regulatory framework for sustainable mobility in the region. although this protocol has not yet been accepted by all eight alpine states, we will endeavour to ensure that it can be ratified by the other alpine states in a short time and that ratification of the 'protocol on transport' becomes one of the main priorities of the european commission.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the florin david report on interoperability solutions for european public administrations (isa), which aims to support cooperation between european public administrations. this programme facilitates effective and efficient cross-border and cross-sectoral electronic interaction between european administrations to enable the provision of e-public services that can facilitate the implementation of community activities and policies for citizens and businesses. this will facilitate the free movement, establishment and work of citizens in the member states without obstacles, and will provide citizens and public administrations with better, more efficient and easily accessible services. i believe that international cooperation should be encouraged and that the isa programme should also be open to the participation of the countries of the european economic area and the candidate countries. they agree to encourage cooperation with other third countries and international organisations or bodies. the participation of the candidate countries in the isa programme is a fundamental step in preparing the public administration of these states for the tasks and working methods entailed by eu accession. i think that we need to look more closely at the possibility of using pre-accession funds to facilitate the participation of the applicant countries in the isa programme.
in writing. - my vote is in favour. the environmental and health effects of pesticide use have been debated at european level and the european parliament has adopted directives on the authorisation and sale of pesticides. this measure lays down the essential health and safety requirements to be met by pesticide application machines placed on the internal market in order to enjoy free circulation within the community. the legislation, in addition to protecting consumers, is aimed at protecting the health and safety of operators. the costs incurred by manufacturers will probably be passed on to users through price increases, but the resulting average annual reduction in pesticide consumption will allow users to make savings that will offset any price increases. the proposed directive achieves the objective of ensuring a common level of environmental protection while avoiding a fragmented regulatory framework at community level, which can generate high costs for companies wishing to operate also beyond national borders.
in writing. - the aim of the proposal for a regulation under consideration, namely to ensure community control of compliance with the rules of the common fisheries policy through its own agency, is certainly worthwhile and meets the many requests made over the years by the european parliament and the european commission. the regulation also suggests - albeit timidly - that the same rules should be implemented and applied uniformly in the 27 member states. while i share the spirit behind the text (supporting the culture of respect for the rules for the correct application of the common fisheries policy), i note that, unfortunately, on this occasion too, the specific features of mediterranean fisheries have not been taken into account. just to give you an example: the obligation to install a satellite vessel monitoring system (vms) on vessels over 10 metres in length may be acceptable for large-sized north sea vessels, but not for small mediterranean vessels, often without cabins, which are often engaged in what is known as 'small-scale fishing'. the problem of the high costs involved is also raised, but this could be overcome with 80% community co-financing, as appropriately suggested in amendment no 20.
the next item is the commission statement on the earthquake in the abruzzo region of italy.
vice-president of the commission. − mr president, the commission sends its condolences to all families who have lost their loved ones in the recent earthquake in italy. the commission has been in close contact with the italian civil protection authorities since the first hours after the earthquake. member states started offering their help through the community civil protection mechanism at a very early stage of the disaster. while this earthquake was very powerful and brought a lot of destruction, national resources were able to cope with the immediate disaster response. however, on 10 april italy made a request for technical experts who could support the country in analysing the stability of buildings damaged by the earthquake. a team of eight national and commission experts was selected. the team was despatched to the site of the earthquake on 18 april. in addition to the assessment of the stability of the buildings, the team will propose solutions with regard to damaged buildings. the commission is currently cooperating with the italian authorities in order to identify options for other eu support. possibilities may include the eu solidarity fund and the reprogramming of the structural and rural development funds. this earthquake is a tragic reminder that natural disasters are a continual threat for all member states. over the last decade earthquakes, heat waves, forest fires, floods and storms have killed many people in europe and destroyed costly infrastructure and precious natural spaces. the member states and the community need to combine their strength to prevent disasters and their impacts and to ensure a rapid and effective european response to major disasters. experience has shown that an integrated and multi-hazard approach should be taken to develop effective measures in both in prevention and in direct response to disasters, as outlined in the commission communication of march 2008 on reinforcing the union’s disaster-response capacity. furthermore, in february 2009 the commission adopted a community approach on the prevention of natural and man-made disasters that represents the state of the art and paves a way for future commission initiatives. it suggests improving the consistency of existing prevention instruments and complementing them, thus reinforcing the added value of eu action. the commission would welcome feedback from the european parliament on the approach proposed in this important communication. furthermore, thanks to the preparatory action on an eu rapid response capability introduced by the european parliament in the 2008 and 2009 budgets, the commission is currently testing, with the member states, ways to improve the overall immediate response capacity of the eu. together, these initiatives are contributing to shaping a genuine european disaster management policy for all types of disaster.

in the period 2002-2007, earthquakes were the fourth most frequent natural disaster in the european union. after this tragedy in abruzzo, which is unfortunately very serious, we must face these tragic events, which are common to many member states, together. the european solidarity fund and the community civil protection mechanism are now in place: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to the full. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the programme to include the mediterranean countries, the countries of the former soviet union and the countries of central and eastern europe. the magnitude of this earthquake and the damage caused are not yet quantifiable: abruzzo needs urgent and substantial measures which the italian government has been taking in a timely and comprehensive manner since the earthquake. however, these measures need european coordination, while respecting national and local competences. on 14 november 2007, parliament unanimously adopted a resolution on the regional impact of earthquakes, concerning the prevention and management of damage caused by such tragic events. this document must become the basis for a coordinated european policy on this subject, is the content of the written question proposed by mr vakalis and some fifty other co-signatories. we therefore hope that the european commission will take up the contents of this resolution and apply them to a european agenda for earthquake prevention and management.

the rapporteur. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, with the adoption of the legislation on air, rail, sea and inland waterway transport by mr teychenné, with this proposal on passenger rights in bus transport, the european union completes the legislative framework for all modes of transport. in drawing up this regulation, we have had to strike a balance between two approaches: the first considers the so-called level planning field for all modes of transport, i.e. different modes of transport can compete on the same terms and with equal opportunities, and at the same time passengers have a high level of protection regardless of the means of transport they have chosen. the second approach reflects the different characteristics of each mode of transport and considers the specificities of each mode, for example the management of liability for delays, in the case of bus transport, on the road, and thus accidents, congestion and so on, compared to rail transport with a dedicated track. i would add two points of reflection and commentary which are in contrast to each other, and for which we have sought, and i believe have achieved, a balance. the real purpose of this , acting president of the council. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i am very honoured to be here with you today to take part in the debate on some of the important public health issues on proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on the application of patients' rights in crossborder healthcare from the council's point of view. the czech presidency is fully aware of the need to ensure legal certainty for patients who receive healthcare in another member state and has also followed up on the work of the french presidency in this respect. our aim is to seek the adoption of such a text that is comprehensible and clear to the citizens of the european union, respects primary law, including the principle of subsidiarity, and fulfils the declared aim of establishing legal certainty for eu citizens in the exercise of their rights to cross-border healthcare. at the same time, however, due account must be taken of the possible impact of the implementation of this proposal on the stability of the health systems of the member states of the european union. given the crucial importance of the proposal, discussions in the council's working bodies are very intensive and ongoing. i am therefore not yet in a position to tell you whether the council will reach a political agreement at the end of the czech presidency, i.e. at the epsco council in june. but i will now make a few general points. the future directive should codify all the case law of the european court of justice concerning the application of the principle of free movement of goods and services in the field of public health, complement the regulation on the coordination of social systems and provide for the possibility for member states to make the receipt of healthcare in another member state conditional on prior consent or the possibility of applying a 'gate-keeping' system. these principles are also reflected in the report by mr bowis on the draft directive which you are debating. it is also possible to identify other themes that are common to the european parliament and the council: the importance of providing patients with complete and accurate information on the possibilities of receiving cross-border healthcare, or the emphasis on ensuring high quality and safety of care. the czech presidency appreciates the consistency of parliament in preparing this report, the wording of which is based on numerous difficult but fruitful discussions in several committees with substantive responsibilities. i am aware that the text of the report represents a compromise between the various political groups and that it has not been easy to achieve, and i would therefore like to thank all those who have contributed to its production, directive. the council shall examine in detail the text of the report and any adopted amendments and give careful consideration to their inclusion in the council common position in order to promote consensus at second reading. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, as i have already said, it is still too early to say whether the epsco council will reach political agreement on the draft directive in june, as the discussions based on the compromise proposal put forward by the czech presidency are not yet over. in any event, the council will continue to discuss this subject, in the light of the report adopted by the european parliament.
member of the commission. − mr president, before i speak about patients’ rights in cross-border health care, let me pay a special tribute to the rapporteur, mr john bowis, who unfortunately is not with us today, but to whom we owe so much on this file. i wish him a speedy recovery and also health and happiness after so many years of excellent service to european citizens. (applause) i also want to thank all the shadow rapporteurs for their constructive work, and of course mr bushill-matthews, who is speaking today on behalf of mr bowis. yesterday, here in strasbourg, we celebrated european patients’ rights day. in doing so, we acknowledged the growing role of patients in health care and recognised the importance of patients having both confidence and knowledge about the care they receive. the central question in this context is: what can the european union do for patients? we have the opportunity this morning to take a major step forward towards building a europe for patients, for each and every european citizen that you, honourable members, represent. first, i must say that i very much appreciate the hard work undertaken by parliament on the examination of the proposal for a directive on patients’ rights in cross-border health care which will shortly be submitted to your vote. let me thank and congratulate you all for your interesting and often challenging debates and for a very efficient process. allow me to recall briefly the rationale behind this proposed directive, as well as its main objectives and principles. the origin of the proposal lies in a decade of jurisprudence of the european court of justice, which ruled that patients have the right to be reimbursed for health care received abroad, even if they could have received that health care at home. this is important. this is a right that the treaty directly grants to eu citizens. however, if the rulings were clear for the individuals concerned, the question of how they apply to all other cases was obscure. therefore, the need for a legislative framework became apparent, so that all patients in europe can exercise their right to reimbursement of cross-border health care. this right should not only be for patients who have access to information that is not publicly available and who can afford a lawyer. therefore, after in-depth reflection and broad consultation, the commission adopted, on 2 july last year, its proposal for a directive. first and foremost, its overall aim is to provide patients with better opportunities and access to health care across europe. patients are at the very heart of this draft law, which also fully respects the diversity of health systems across europe. let me be clear on this. i know many fears have been expressed, but this legislation will not impose changes in the organisation and financing of national health systems. the proposed directive has three main objectives: first, to clarify the conditions under which patients will be reimbursed at the home country tariff for cross-border health care; second, to give assurance about the quality and safety of care throughout europe; and third, to foster european cooperation among health-care systems. on the basis of these three pillars, much can be done for our citizens, primarily for those who want to seek cross-border health care, but, beyond this, for all patients across europe. i look forward to your debate.
the committee on employment and social affairs has adopted a number of amendments to the proposal. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, how can we define this directive? an opportunity for patients to choose appropriate care and quick access to services; an opportunity for regional health systems to improve the quality and effectiveness of their health service; the commission has also proposed a number of measures to improve the quality of services provided to the public. european reference networks, standards on technologies, development of telemedicine, will develop crossborder cooperation already under way. this requires an appropriate information system, monitoring of the quality and efficiency of health facilities, a guarantee of the professional ethics of healthcare workers, and a non-bureaucratic way of regulating cross-border mobility. the directive is a balanced response to these needs.
on behalf of the uen group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, today we are adopting a very important directive, a directive which concerns patients, as has already been said, and which concerns all european citizens. on the eve of the european elections, all european citizens can once again see how parliament can have a positive impact on their lives. the charter of fundamental rights of the european union affirms the right to health care, and today we are giving this right substance with this directive. a recent eurobarometer survey highlights that 50% of european citizens are already willing to travel abroad for treatment in the hope of finding better and faster treatment for their illness, and 74% of citizens believe that if they go abroad for treatment, they will be reimbursed by their member state. currently, only national rules govern the matter, and the public is poorly informed about the possibilities, reimbursements and treatment available abroad. in fact, today only 4% of european citizens seek treatment abroad. the european union has a uniform regulation only in the case of treatment for medical emergencies which have occurred abroad on the basis of the european health insurance card regulation. today parliament is responding positively to the demand for health protection from european citizens, and europe is also preparing to break down frontiers in the field of health care and give all patients the opportunity to choose where they want to be treated!

member of the commission. − mr president, as we have seen once again today, parliament’s debates on this matter are both rich and passionate. its discussions add a great deal to the commission’s initiative, and the amendments on which it is to vote will also constitute a most valuable input on a number of key aspects. on patients’ rights to quality and safe health care, many of you have confirmed the fundamental importance of securing clarity and assurances. i fully agree, and very much hope that this ambition will be confirmed. on the question of assumption of the costs of treatment abroad, clear concerns have been expressed about the inability of a significant number of patients to afford cross-border health care. indeed, this is an important and most valid point. inequalities of revenue clearly exist throughout europe, and this has serious consequences in relation to access to a number of fundamental services, including health care. this issue has to be addressed. however, reducing such inequalities is a difficult challenge, and even more difficult against the backdrop of the current economic crisis. it will require a significant and coordinated effort from the eu and the member states at all levels. unfortunately, what we can do in the context of the draft directive is limited. the commission proposal leaves the door open for member states to offer direct assumption of the costs of cross-border treatment, for example with a system of written confirmation of the amount that will be paid. if parliament wants this to be clear in the text, i can only welcome it. the proposed directive did not seek to prevent this, but is careful to respect member states’ responsibilities in organising health care. that is why we were cautious to limit the financial impact of cross-border health care on national health systems and sickness insurance funds. however, the two objectives are not incompatible. it would be up to the member states to reconcile them as far as possible to the benefit of the patients, in particular those with modest revenues. regarding the relationship of this directive with the social security regulation, we agree, i believe, on the need for clear articulation, which would mean that, once prior authorisation is requested by a patient, and if the conditions of the regulation are fulfilled – in other words, when there is undue delay – the regulation should apply. it has to be crystal clear that this means the tariffs of the regulation shall apply so that patients can benefit from the most advantageous system. regarding prior authorisation for hospital care, the proposed provisions are based on two kinds of consideration. firstly, case-law: the court has ruled that such a system could be justified under certain circumstances. we have codified this in article 8(3). secondly, it would not be appropriate to go beyond such provisions with a looser – or indeed unconditional – system of prior authorisation, legally or de facto generalised in all member states. we all know that patient mobility will remain a very limited phenomenon. this means that its budgetary impact will also be limited. therefore, there is no need to construct unnecessary barriers for patients. prior authorisation for hospital treatment has to remain a safeguard mechanism, applicable when justified. against this background, systems of prior notification as proposed by the rapporteur could amount to indirect – and indeed unnecessary – control of patients, impeding rather than facilitating the process. i understand that the rationale behind this suggestion was not to achieve such an outcome, but believe that this would actually restrict patients’ rights as defined by the court. such administrative mechanisms run the risk of being both cumbersome and arbitrary. i am concerned at the suggestion regarding the definition of hospital care. this definition is indeed a key point for patients’ rights as it sets the boundary for the prior authorisation system. we have proposed to define the concept of hospital care through a community list based on the shared understanding of experts, who would take account of the development of technologies. this would allow for a reasonable and modern approach to the concept of hospital care. some of you are calling for national lists to be drawn up independently, and most member states are calling for that as well. a definition based on national lists would actually lead to discrepancies as to what constitutes hospital care in each member state, with a considerable risk of eroding patients’ rights. if we were to go down this road, we would need to have such lists based on clearly defined criteria and subjected to a review process. otherwise, patients’ rights, as defined by the european judges, would be undermined. some of you have said that, if we adopt this proposed directive, only a few patients would profit from it, and that they would be the very few informed patients. on the contrary, i believe that under this directive we are giving the opportunity and the right to every single patient, before he or she leaves home, to be fully informed in order to be able to make an informed choice. i understand the concerns raised regarding the difficulty of getting clear information on health professionals when seeking health care abroad. this is simply a question of patient safety. here, we need to agree on practical solutions which also respect a number of key principles, such as the right to personal data protection and the presumption of innocence. i am sure that common ground can be found on the basis of your preliminary suggestions. reference was made to amendment 67 on relaxation of the rule for affiliations to social security systems. unfortunately, this cannot be accepted. regarding the legal basis for the proposed directive, many of you would like to add article 152 to article 95. i understand that this is an important issue for some of the political groups, but it is difficult to have definite views at this stage of the examination of the directive. it is important to assess this issue in the light of the evolution of the text, in order to decide what the appropriate legal basis is. clearly, if the content of the final text justifies it, the addition of article 152 to article 95 could certainly be considered. i remain open to considering this at any future stage of the codecision process. (applause) some of you have again raised the issue of the possible excessive inflow of patients from other member states, and of how the receiving health system would be protected. my reply is the same as the one i would give to those who fear excessive outflows in the absence of prior authorisation for hospital care, which is that the intention of this proposal is not to promote patient mobility. as i have said, mobility of patients is a limited phenomenon and we do not expect this to change. therefore, it would be simply disproportionate to give carte blanche to member states to take measures to refuse patients in order to control inflows. member states have to ensure that patients from other member states are not discriminated against. any form of control of incoming patients would have to be assessed as to whether it would amount to an acceptable exception to the principle of non-discrimination on the basis of nationality set out in the eu treaty. regarding patients suffering from rare diseases, i understand that you are looking for the best approach in order for them to benefit from the health care they need, but sometimes the best is the enemy of the good. today, you will vote on mr trakatellis’ report, which concerns the recent strategy that the commission has already set out on rare diseases, and includes the proposed council recommendation. as you know, for these conditions, quick diagnosis and access to treatment are complex and not always possible or available at home. therefore, in order to bring the benefits of european cooperation to patients with rare diseases, they really need to be included in this directive on patients’ rights in cross-border health care. i think that there is broad agreement on the need for european cooperation on centres of reference for rare diseases, for example. i would therefore urge you to keep rare diseases in the scope of the directive. regarding the proposed exclusion of organ transplantation, i simply cannot agree. transplantation is a medical procedure and it is difficult to justify why patients should not have the right to benefit from it as cross-border health care, as ruled by the court. however, the issue of organ allocation is a different matter. i have therefore asked experts in the commission to look into this question to see how organ allocation could be dealt with in a different context. today, we can take an important step forward towards the adoption of this directive. now that we are just a matter of weeks away from the next european elections, allow me to pay tribute to this parliament and to its administration for all the efforts made to make this vote today possible, for which i thank you all. let me also once again thank mr bowis and the shadow rapporteurs for their efforts and hard work and wish him a speedy recovery. we hope to see him back soon to take up his duties and a normal life. in writing. - thank you, mr president. my vote is in favour. regulation (ec) no 2560/2001 focuses on cross-border transfers and cross-border electronic payment transactions. this regulation was adopted on 19 december 2001 and aims to ensure that the cost of a crossborder payment is the same as that of a payment made within a member state. until 1 january 2006, it applied only to transfers, withdrawals from atms and payments made by debit and credit card up to an amount of eur 12 500 in eu countries, whereas from that date, it can be made up to an amount of eur 50 000. this change has led to lower prices and increased competition in the payment services markets. however, regulation (ec) no 2560/2001 also has limitations, such as the lack of definition of 'corresponding payments' and the lack of the review clause, which should be addressed immediately. we conclude by saying that we support the proposals to update and amend regulation (ec) no 2560/2001, as it is our duty to make cross-border payment transactions easier and cheaper.

that the european parliament has given to the commission's proposals, which form part of the work-life balance package adopted last autumn. achieving a balance between work, family and private life is, as you know, one of the priorities of the commission's gender equality plan. strengthening policies addressing this issue is essential to increase women's participation in the labour market, to address the challenges of changing family structures and population ageing, and to promote equal treatment for men and women. in this context, i believe that it is necessary to improve the legislation on maternity and parental leave. it is also of the utmost importance to improve the situation of self-employed women. i am very pleased with the progress made on both commission legislative proposals. i am also pleased that the negotiations between the social partners on parental leave were successful. i hope to be able to present a formal proposal before the summer holidays to make their agreement binding. let me briefly recall the objectives of the commission's proposal to amend the maternity leave directive: to promote a high level of maternal health and safety protection, to encourage women to have as many children as they want and, at the same time, to promote women's participation in the labour market. in this respect, the commission proposal seeks in particular to extend maternity leave from 14 to 18 weeks, to increase the maternity allowance so that women can take time off work to care for their children and feel financially secure, to give women more flexibility in the arrangements for maternity leave and the working conditions for re-entry into employment. i am aware of the difficulties in striking the right balance between increasing protection and making these additional measures economically acceptable to employers and member states. mr president, madam member, ladies and gentlemen, the commission welcomes the many amendments tabled by the european parliament which help to strengthen or clarify the proposal. these include: amendment 11 on demographic trends, amendment 25 stressing the need for better reconciliation of work and family life, amendment 50 on support for member states in promoting part-time work, amendment 35 on the optional maternity leave before childbirth and amendment 53 clarifying that women on maternity leave may be paid a higher salary, and amendment 56 on workers' pension rights. the commission is also prepared to accept a number of other amendments, either in principle or in full, and i welcome the amendment which would allow, under certain conditions, parental leave to be counted as maternity leave. such provisions would take into account differences between member states and would favour those member states with developed family leave systems, such as the nordic countries. however, i would like to avoid a situation where the revision of directive 92/85/eec is used to introduce topics that should be addressed in another context. in my view, this would undermine the objectives of the commission's proposal, which are firstly to increase the protection of mothers and secondly to promote women's participation in the labour market. therefore, while i fully support your proposal to introduce a paternity leave provision i do not think that the current directive aimed at protecting mothers is the appropriate instrument for this. the commission would therefore reject the amendments relating to paternity leave. nevertheless, the commission considers it appropriate to address this issue in the future, also in the light of the final text of the agreement between the european social partners on parental leave. i was also pleased to note parliament's request to introduce leave for adoption of a child (amendment 44). the idea is correct, but i think that a revision of directive 92/85/eec is not the right way to go. we have to recognize that the situation of the mother who adopts a child is different. however, as with paternity leave, the commission considers it appropriate to address this issue at a later stage, in particular in the context of parental leave. mr president, madam member, ladies and gentlemen, the commission welcomes your proposal for 20 weeks of maternity leave. this is in line with the logic of the commission proposal, which allows for more than 18 weeks of leave in a number of different cases. however, the impact of this extension should be reflected in the other provisions of the commission's proposal: as regards breastfeeding, a woman on 18 weeks' maternity leave would have sufficient time to breastfeed her child and not have to adjust her working hours to this. in those circumstances, i would not be in favour of introducing a legal obligation to regulate the working hours of breastfeeding women. instead, i would urge member states to consider whether additional measures are needed to allow women to continue breastfeeding after 18 weeks of maternity leave. similarly, in the case of maternity allowance, the commission proposal introduces the principle of full pay. in fact, many member states already apply this principle. the commission proposal also allows member states to set a maximum level for this contribution. the commission is not in favour of parliament's proposal to pay full salary for a certain period and to introduce a maximum for the remainder of maternity leave, as this would discourage mothers from taking full maternity leave. the commission therefore does not recommend the amendments concerned. the commission also considers that some of the proposed amendments either weaken the effects of the proposal, introduce too many details or go beyond the scope of this directive. this is the case, for example, with amendment no 30 concerning the right to refuse night work. i believe that a pregnant or breastfeeding woman should be able to refuse to work at night at any time without having to give a reason. the has been established by the european court of justice. the commission cannot therefore accept amendment no 68. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i would now like to deal in more detail with mrs commission has also proposed a large number of amendments which it can accept in full or in principle. these amendments generally clarify the commission proposal and thus seek greater legal certainty. i would point out, however, that the commission cannot accept amendment no 14 concerning social protection for assisting spouses. i understand that this is an important aspect for the european parliament. however, this amendment raises certain problems. in particular, the voluntary approach introduced in the commission proposal represents a substantial improvement compared to the current situation. the commission proposal imposes a legal obligation on member states to ensure that assisting spouses enjoy, on request, a level of protection equivalent to that enjoyed by selfemployed persons. the compulsory inclusion of assisting spouses in the social protection system would also have significant financial implications. in times of economic crisis, it is important to ensure that businesses, and in particular small family businesses, do not incur additional costs against their will. so i think we should give the assistant husbands or wives a choice. and this amendment would in writing. - my vote is in favour. pursuant to regulation (ec) no 1234/2007, poultry meat may be sold on the international market even if it has undergone antimicrobial treatments. in june 2008, after several attempts, the european parliament succeeded in passing a resolution banning this type of marketing. the commission has not complied with the resolution, as the us only exports poultrymeat to the eu that has been treated with chemicals or antimicrobials. this strategy is at odds with the investments made by poultry professionals in their field and made in accordance with community legislation, which requires that, in order to reduce the risks of contamination of meat, only eu-approved protection methods, such as cold treatment, should be used. we therefore support the following amendments to regulation (ec) no 1234/2007: 1) withdrawal of recital 5 of the commission's preamble, which states that 'the exclusive reference to cold treatment in the definition of 'poultrymeat' is too restrictive in relation to technological developments'. that definition should therefore be adapted; 2) replacement of recital 5 by a new recital which provides for the monitoring of the origin of meat in order to inform and ensure transparency for the consumer; (3) maintenance of the 'cold method' protection treatment only.

member of the commission. − madam president, the world of rosé wine has a long, long history, but there is no definition of rosé wine within eu legislation or within the international organisation of vine and wine (oiv). they all remain silent. in certain regions, wine-makers have invested a lot of effort to develop a high-quality rosé wine based on a precise product specification, and have limited the wine-making practices for rosé wine to traditional methods. however, other protected designations of origin (pdos) do not impose restrictions on making rosé wine. the product specification of champagne allows the blending of red and white to produce rosé champagne. at eu level, the ban on blending red and white wine is today limited to the production of table wine. the discussion on wine-making practices, including on blending, started back in 2006 during the negotiations on the wine reform. with the reform, the commission gained competence to authorise new oenological practices and shall base itself on the oiv’s recommendations. following wide-ranging discussions which took place last autumn with stakeholders and with all member states, the commission proposed the abolition of the ban on blending red and white wine. this was subject to an indicative vote in the wine regulatory committee in january when a majority of member states, including france, voted in favour. the draft regulation has been notified to the world trade organisation under the procedure in the agreement on technical barriers to trade, and we have recently accepted further time for third countries to examine our proposal. therefore, the regulation will be formally voted by the wine regulatory committee later in june, most probably on 19 june, because further delay would prevent us from implementing the new oenological practices from 1 august this year, as foreseen by the council regulation. you also asked for a specific impact assessment before the removal of the blending prohibition. in-depth impact assessments were carried out by the commission’s services when drafting the wine reform and we do not therefore intend to restart the work undertaken in 2006 and 2007 to prepare the wine reform, nor to make an in-depth impact assessment of all different individual wine-making practices, so we base ourselves on the work that is taking place in the oiv. already now, economists in the wine sector stress that this reform will not weaken traditional rosés as these rosés with an appellation are not in competition with table wines. it is clear that the traditional rosé is a quality product that is highly appreciated by consumers and associated with the place of origin of this product. allowing the blending of table wine will lead to fair competition between european countries and third countries since we have allowed third countries – as already mentioned here today – to do this blending. i completely agree with mrs laperrouze. why should we put our wine producers in a worse competitive situation than those that can sell wine within the european union? some weeks ago, i had a meeting here in strasbourg with rosé wine producers from provence in france member of the commission. − mr president, i want to thank honourable members, first of all, for a very serious and substantive debate on the democratic process in turkey, and i also want this evening to thank the european parliament for its contribution to the eu’s policy in relation to turkey. there has been critical but constructive support for our engagement with turkey in a very critical period. i think parliament’s approach – like, i trust, the commission’s approach – can be described as fair and firm in relation to turkey and its eu accession process. indeed, in my view, we have to be fair and firm and only by being both at the same time can we achieve results. what i mean is that we have to be fair in the sense of maintaining the eu perspective as the critical driver of reforms in the country, keeping our word concerning turkey’s chance to show that it will be able to meet eu accession criteria. at the same time, we have to be firm by applying rigorous conditionality, especially as regards fundamental freedoms and democratic principles. these two key elements – fairness and firmness – only work together and they cannot be separated from each other. i think that is clearly the best way of supporting a democratic transformation in turkey, which is our objective, because it makes turkey a better partner and a prospective possible member state of the european union, in line with the negotiating framework adopted in the early hours of 4 october 2005. the current state of affairs is pretty much a mixed picture, as joost lagendijk, the chair of the european parliament delegation to the eu-turkey joint parliamentary committee, described it. sometimes it feels like two steps forward and one step backward, but better that way than vice versa. as mr duff raised the issue, i think that the ergenekon investigation is a case in point. in view of the investigation so far, it seems that it was essential that this network behind potential political or other attacks against democracy in turkey was revealed and will continue to be revealed in the spirit of the rule of law and democratic secularism. on the other hand, in the recent stages of the ergenekon investigation, one may question whether all the principles of the rule of law have been truly applied or whether there are some other political purposes behind these arrests. the jury is still out. we are following this very closely and we shall certainly report on this in our forthcoming progress report in the coming autumn. in my view, three principles are particularly important. first of all, the democratic principles: pursuing constitutional reform, where reform of the rules governing political parties is essential in view of the experiences of last year, this year and previous years, when we have seen the pitfalls of the constitutional framework of turkey in this regard, as pointed out by the venice commission of the council of europe. second, freedom of expression, which graf lambsdorff referred to, is the bedrock of democracy. this was discussed quite recently at the meeting of parliament’s joint parliamentary committee with the turkish grand national assembly. i am concerned about media freedom and its development in turkey and we will certainly come back to this as a special section in our progress report in the coming autumn. yes, there has been positive progress concerning the consequences of the reform of the infamous article 301 some one or two years ago. on the other hand, relative progress concerning article 301 does not justify attacks on media freedom elsewhere, as has been referred to in several statements this evening. finally, the rule of law, which is underpinning the functioning of all society and the economy and which is the key value of the european union: that is illustrated in the fight against terrorism, which we support, as long as it is conducted in line with the rule of law and principles of justice in the best european tradition. so, the pace of negotiations with turkey will essentially depend on the progress and intensity of the reforms enhancing fundamental freedoms and the rule of law in the country, in all walks of life and all corners of the country. that is the foundation of the negotiation process. progress in the technical negotiations will depend on whether there is serious progress in, and intensity and implementation of, these reforms enhancing fundamental freedoms and human rights and democratic secularism. these are enshrined in the treaty on european union and in our common european values. that is the critical yardstick of turkish progress towards the european union.

the agenda includes the report by janusz wojciechowski, on behalf of the committee on agriculture and rural development, on the proposal for a council regulation on the protection of animals at the time of slaughter (com (2008) 0553 - c6-0451/2008 - 2008/0180 (cns)) (a6-0185/2009).
member of the commission. − mr president, i would like to thank the european parliament and in particular the rapporteur, mr wojciechowski, for having supported the main elements of the commission proposal on the protection of animals at the time of killing. in particular, i am pleased that the european parliament accepted the general approach of the proposal, which is to ensure the animal welfare legislation applicable to slaughterhouses is in line with the hygiene package which was adopted back in 2004. the current legislation on the protection of animals at slaughter dates back to 1993 and is clearly not in line with the latest developments in the areas of food safety, animal health and animal welfare. under the current proposal, slaughterhouse operators will have to establish standard operating procedures, rely on welfare indicators for stunning, and personnel will have to receive training on animal welfare. on the issue of religious slaughter, i would like to stress that the commission fully shares the attachment of the european parliament to freedom of religion and to underline that the commission’s intention is to maintain the status quo on this sensitive matter. the treaty clearly states the need to take into account practices related to religion in the formulation of community policy. it is clear that there are many different practices regarding religious slaughter across the member states of the union. the commission suggests that subsidiarity should be maintained in this area. it has worked well for the past 15 years and should continue to work well in the future. in this respect, we can accept in principle, subject to rewording, amendments that reflect the approach of the current legislation, which preserves the right of freedom of religion while allowing member states to adopt or maintain stricter rules. in this regard, i would note that there seems to be agreement in council along these lines. i would now like to say a few words on the practice of backyard slaughter. today, the slaughter of animals for private consumption is permitted outside slaughterhouses (except cattle), but pigs, sheep and goats must have previously been stunned. some citizens in the member states traditionally slaughter pigs for christmas and lambs for easter. the preservation of these traditions is important to the commission but there is no need to derogate from the stunning of animals, thereby undermining the welfare of the animals. therefore the commission believes that prior stunning should always be performed when pigs or lambs are slaughtered outside slaughterhouses. another point of the proposal is related to the establishment of a national centre of reference. we believe that this element is essential to guarantee proper enforcement of the proposed measures. in slaughterhouses, official inspectors perform food safety controls, mainly on carcasses. they have little time and limited competences to assess animal welfare parameters. these days, stunning equipment is complex and difficult to evaluate in relation to their welfare efficiency. national reference centres would meet the need for technical and scientific information on the welfare of animals at slaughter and the commission considers that this requirement should be maintained in the proposal. the commission also believes that certificates of competence required for the personnel in slaughterhouses should be issued following an independent examination. this system has been developed in other areas of animal welfare, both in the public and the private sector. where this has been properly implemented, it has provided good results. this should therefore be extended to all eu slaughterhouses. animals are also killed in huge numbers outside slaughterhouses in order to control the spread of disease. it is true that requirements already exist for animal health purposes, but today’s requirements do not relate to animal welfare. people consider that mass culling for disease-control purposes should be performed in the most humane way possible. transparency, which means proper reporting, is therefore essential. furthermore, previous experience in these emergency situations has shown that it is crucial to collect information on good practices and on mistakes that might have occurred. proper monitoring and reporting on animal welfare should therefore be required in cases of mass culling. i would very much welcome your support of the commission proposal. if successfully adopted, the european union would have the potential to lead and innovate globally on animal welfare.

the rapporteur. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, first of all i would like to express my sincere thanks to all those, all the colleagues and officials who have worked together to improve the text we are going to vote on tomorrow. i would like to thank mr demetriou in particular, whose excellent recommendation i have just heard inspired my report. i have always worked with the need to provide useful guidance for the construction of a genuine european area of judicial cooperation in mind and i hope, indeed i am convinced, that my work will be useful to the next swedish presidency, which will have the difficult task of drawing up the stockholm programme. in drafting the text, i took two basic considerations as my starting point: the first is that criminal proceedings have numerous and important implications for the fundamental freedoms of both victims of crime and of the suspects and accused. the priority, therefore, which this parliament cannot fail to stress, the main point of my report, is the attention to respect for human rights. the recommendation devotes a great deal of attention to the defence of fundamental rights, with particular reference to the protection of victims, prison conditions, the rights of prisoners, procedural guarantees, including the right to a statement of rights and to the assistance of an ombudsman, the right to evidence, the right to be informed of the nature and grounds of the accusation and to have access to relevant documents in an understandable language, and therefore the right to an interpreter. the second consideration i am guided by is that, as the report on the implementation of the 2007 hague programme shows, the level of implementation in judicial cooperation in criminal matters has been rather low, while satisfactory developments have been recorded in other areas, such as cooperation in civil matters, border management, immigration, asylum policies. clearly, then, more must be done. the principle of mutual recognition, the cornerstone of judicial cooperation, is far from being satisfactorily implemented. we must get to the root of the problem, identify the causes of this low growth, so that we can devise the most effective solutions. the main causes, i believe, lie in the lack of mutual knowledge and trust between the states, which is why i emphasize in the report training, evaluation, exchange of information and good practice. as regards training, it is certainly not necessary to forget the considerable progress made, in particular thanks to the training support provided by the european judicial training network. however, in my view, we need to move beyond the current training model based mainly on national vocational schools to build a stronger common legal culture which is still lacking. i therefore felt the need to move towards a european training institute for judges and lawyers, well structured, with adequate resources, but stressing the need to avoid unnecessary duplication with what already exists and to give the national schools an important role. the second point: the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. the proposal is therefore to set up a group of experts to monitor the application of community law and the quality and efficiency of justice on a permanent basis, on the model of the schengen mutual evaluation system. the aim is also to identify any weaknesses and legislative gaps in the area of judicial cooperation in criminal matters, so as to provide the european legislator with all the information tools necessary for a correct policy and regulatory assessment. finally, the use of new technologies, which is very important for data collection, strengthening existing banking systems and the circulation of information. i hope that tomorrow's vote will be a repeat of the excellent result achieved in the libe committee.

services are studying in depth. i would add that community legislation requires member states to conduct border control operations in accordance with the principle of non-refoulement. this principle means that a state must refrain from returning people to a territory where they could be subjected to torture, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment. in the case of asylum seekers and refugees, deportation cannot take place where their lives, their freedom may be threatened because of their race, religion or nationality. in short, we ensure that this duty of protection is respected. finally,
